title: Chrome DevTools documentation: Elements/CSS, Console, JavaScript debugging, Overrides
authors: Chrome DevTools team (Google), Kayce Basques and Sofia Emelianova
why_trusted: The official documentation of Chrome DevTools, hosted on developer.chrome.com by the Chrome team that builds the tool; the pages read today cover CSS inspection, the Console and its utilities API, breakpoints, source maps and local overrides.

title: ECMA-426: Source map format specification
authors: Ecma International TC39-TG4 (editors Asumu Takikawa, Nicolo Ribaudo, Jon Kuperman)
why_trusted: The Ecma International standard for the source map format that DevTools, bundlers and compilers follow; the full text is freely readable and the live page is dated 11 November 2026.

title: Chrome DevTools: Network features reference
authors: Kayce Basques, Sofia Emelianova (Chrome DevTools team)
why_trusted: The official Chrome DevTools reference for the Network panel on developer.chrome.com, written by the Chrome team; it lists the timing phases Queueing, Stalled, DNS Lookup, Initial connection, Request sent, Waiting (TTFB) and Content Download, plus throttling and HAR export.

title: Chrome DevTools: Fix memory problems and heap snapshots
why_trusted: The official Chrome DevTools guide to memory leaks; covers detached DOM nodes, allocation timelines, heap snapshots, the Retainers section and the Comparison view.

title: Chrome DevTools: Performance, Application, Coverage, Rendering and Recorder docs
why_trusted: Official Chrome DevTools references for the Performance panel (live metrics with CrUX, CPU throttling, layout shifts, insights) and the Application, Coverage, Rendering and Recorder panels.

title: web.dev: Core Web Vitals, long tasks and bfcache
authors: Philip Walton, Jeremy Wagner, Brendan Kenny, Barry Pollard (Google)
why_trusted: web.dev is Google's official web platform guidance site; the Web Vitals article defines the Core Web Vitals thresholds (LCP 2.5 s, INP 200 ms, CLS 0.1) and sibling articles define long tasks (over 50 ms) and bfcache testing.

title: Firefox DevTools User Docs
why_trusted: The official user documentation of Firefox DevTools, hosted on Mozilla's Firefox Source Docs and covering the Grid and Flexbox inspectors, Edit fonts, Accessibility inspector and about:debugging.

title: Web Inspector Reference (WebKit)
why_trusted: The Web Inspector reference published by the WebKit project, which builds Safari's engine and its inspector, including the Enabling Web Inspector page for iOS devices.

title: Get started with remote debugging Android devices
why_trusted: The official Chrome DevTools documentation for debugging Android Chrome from a desktop via chrome://inspect, maintained by the Chrome team.

title: GoogleChrome/lighthouse
why_trusted: The Lighthouse project itself (Apache-2.0), owned by the GoogleChrome organization; its README states Lighthouse is integrated into the Chrome DevTools Lighthouse panel, and its JSON report and trace processing (core/lib/tracehouse) are the formats the capstone CLI reads.

title: ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend
niche_reason: Specialised niche: the browser DevTools UI code itself, the only implementation of Chrome DevTools.
why_trusted: The client side of Chrome DevTools itself (BSD-3-Clause), per its README; the GitHub repo mirrors chromium.googlesource.com, so study only the narrow subtrees front_end/models/trace, front_end/models/har and front_end/panels/network, not the whole tree.
